title: Close an inside-fitting pressure cooker
keywords: oval lid through a smaller mouth
instruction: Close the pressure cooker, ready to go on the stove.
context: Inside-fitting (inner-lid) pressure cookers are an everyday pot in millions of homes. The lid is larger than the oval mouth: it goes in only tilted and crosswise, has to be turned in line inside, and falls back into the cooker unless it is pulled up against the rim and the locking loop is put over the handles.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. The table top is the kitchen counter. (1) A 1.5 litre inside-fitting pressure cooker body (Hawkins Classic CL15, 3.25 mm aluminium), loose on the counter, its axis 34 cm forward and 16 cm right of the centre line: a 130 mm flat base, a 159 mm body, its rim's top 105 mm above the counter, with a 3 mm lip running in to an oval mouth 120 x 138 mm (the long axis across the handle). Body 1.04 kg plus 0.40 kg of rice and water, 22 mm deep (real trial: 95 g of uncooked white rice and 300 ml of room-temperature tap water, fresh each session). A black bakelite body handle (130 x 26 x 28 mm, top 102.5 mm above the counter) on a steel bracket points left and toward the robot at 45 degrees; on the bracket, 93 mm from the cooker's axis, a 6 x 10.5 mm steel pivot post with its top 116.5 mm above the counter; under the handle's end, a hook pocket for the locking loop. (2) The lid, 0.21 kg, lying top up on the counter, its middle 42 cm forward and 38 cm right, its handle pointing toward the robot at right angles to the body handle: an oval aluminium plate 128 x 146 x 2.5 mm (4 mm larger than the mouth all round) edged with a 5 mm black rubber gasket, a vent tube in the middle, a 10 x 8 mm steel handle bar running 150 mm out from the vent tube to a 110 x 22 x 20 mm black bakelite lid handle (its end 25 mm past the body handle's when closed), and, hinged at the lid handle's end, a steel locking loop (3.5 mm wire, 44 mm wide, 60 mm long, 8 g) lying folded out on the counter. Seated, the lid's gasket is up against the underside of the rim's lip, the handle bar lies on the pivot, the lid handle sits 2 mm above the body handle, and the lid's top face is 4.5 mm below the rim's top; with nothing holding it the lid swings down into the cooker about the pivot. Real trial only, prepared once per cooker before its first trial: four pieces of masking tape on the body just below the rim, 45 degrees either side of the body handle and of the far side (the depth marks), and D0, the lid's depth below the rim's top at each mark with the cooker closed by hand as the manual says (lid centralised, handles squeezed, loop in), read once with a caliper's depth rod (4.5 mm in the model). Nothing is wiped or coated on the cooker. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Everything is read on the end state. The run ends once the robot has let go with the locking loop hooked under the body handle's end and kept both hands off for 0.5 s (no part of either hand touching the cooker, the lid or the loop; each gripper at least 5 cm from the lid's handle bar and handle and from the loop), or else at the run limit with the robot stopped where it is, still holding the lid if it holds it. The seated checks are then read, before anyone touches the cooker, the lid, the loop or the robot, and without opening the cooker; the latch-hold pull comes last. The simulation reads the same quantities at the same places, in the same order. Seated, four checks (real trial in brackets): (1) handles together: the lid handle's underside is within 4 mm of the body handle's top, 6 mm in from the body handle's end (a phone on a small stand square to the handles' end, a steel rule standing on the counter behind it: one frame); (2) in line: the middle of the lid handle's end is within 13 mm sideways of the body handle's centre line; (3) centred: the vent tube's centre is within 2.5 mm of the mouth's middle (2 and 3: one photo from directly above, the mouth's 120 x 138 mm as the scale); (4) depth: at four marks 5 mm in from the mouth's edge, 45 degrees either side of the body handle and of the far side, the lid's top face is within 2 mm of D0 below the rim's top (a caliper rested on the rim's top at each tape mark, its depth rod lowered onto the lid; a photo of each reading). D0 is a one-time calibration per cooker (see setup; 4.5 mm in the model), never read during or after a trial. The caliper touches only the rim and, with its rod, the lid's face; the rod can only push the lid down, away from the rim, so it can fail a reading but never create one. A cocked lid reads D0 on its high side and deeper on its low side: any cock over 1.1 degrees puts a mark more than 2 mm deep, and together the four checks put the whole gasket at least 1 mm in under the rim and within 2.5 mm of its underside (both computed on the model). Latched: the loop's crossbar is hooked under the body handle's end (the side frame; sim: the loop swung in 34-50 degrees, its crossbar bearing on the cooker in the pocket). Hands off: as above (video). Latch holds, last and only on a seated, latched lid with the hands off: the lid handle is pulled straight up with 1 N, 10 mm in from its end, for 1 s, and throughout the handles' gap stays within 4 mm, the loop stays hooked and the hands stay off (a spring scale hooked there, pulled to 100 g and held 1 s, filmed by the side camera against the rule). 1.0: seated and latched with the hands off at the end state, and the latch held; 0.5: seated at the end state without that (e.g. the robot still holding the lid up at the run limit, or a failed pull); 0.25: the lid was at some time wholly inside the cooker, below the rim (video); else 0.0. 0.0 for good if, before the trial ends, the cooker tips more than 25 degrees or the cooker or the lid falls off the counter. An unlatched lid swings back into the cooker as soon as it is let go, so it cannot be seated with the hands off. Nothing is read after the pull; the cooker is then opened.
reset_notes: Open the cooker as the manual says (squeeze the handles, swing the loop out, push the lid toward the far wall and take it out the way it went in), wipe the gasket and the rim dry, and lay the lid top up on the counter at its marks, its handle toward the robot and the loop folded out. The tape marks stay on the body and D0 stays with the cooker. Rice and water: replace each session.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz). Real sizes; the mouth, lid and handle sizes are design values from the maker's photos and overall sizes, and the 1.04 kg body is split from the maker's 1.28 kg carton weight. The gasket is rigid, where a real one is squeezed onto the rim; the loop's catch is an arc-shaped pocket, and only pivot friction keeps the latched lid from sliding, so the latch-hold pull is 1 N. Bar rigid on the lid (real: some play). Rice and water: a rigid 0.40 kg layer.
